page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.4xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores based on the Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 600 GB NVMe SSD instance store. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is categorized as weak, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark CPU scores fall within the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also show average performance. Database operations, including Redis SET operations at 13.2 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 11.91 GB/sec, consistently align with average tier expectations.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a balanced allocation of compute, memory, and high-speed local NVMe storage. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require fast local scratch space and moderate network throughput without needing top-tier single-thread performance. The instance is suitable for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale software compilation.
